author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected. The correction opens showing the visit's current date and description, applies the same rules as booking, replaces the details of that same visit rather than booking a second one, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new details and the owner's record is shown.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has no visit it did not have before.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the visit is unchanged.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the visit is unchanged.
non_goals: Any link into the correction from the owner's record; the correction page is reached only by opening it directly.
Changing which pet a visit belongs to.
notes: NG-5 narrowed to cancellation only; recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than resolved: whether the owner's record should offer a way into the correction (a follow-up request is expected), and whether a correction reached through the wrong owner or pet should be refused as booking one is (Visits edge case 1). Neither blocks this slice.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Narrow NG-5 so only cancellation remains out of scope; correcting date/description is now in scope via the new requirement.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction is a third server-rendered form flow in the owner feature package, alongside owner edit and pet edit. It needs no new package, no new pattern, and no new dependency; system-design.md Overview and Package Structure cover the shape unchanged. The one adjustment is to VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, the shared @ModelAttribute("visit") method that runs before every handler in the controller. Today it unconditionally constructs a Visit and calls pet.addVisit(visit). For the correction it must instead resolve the existing visit and add nothing. PetController.findPet already demonstrates the exact pattern: an optional @PathVariable(name=..., required=false) Integer on a shared @ModelAttribute method, branching on null between the new and the edit mapping. Apply that pattern to visitId.
integration_points: VisitController gains GET and POST at /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, named initUpdateVisitForm and processUpdateVisitForm after the PetController initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm pair.

loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId. Null keeps today's behaviour for the /visits/new mappings. Non-null resolves the visit from the pet already loaded in the same call and returns it without calling pet.addVisit.
Pet gains getVisit(Integer id) returning the visit with that id or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). Aggregate navigation belongs on the entity, not as a stream expression in the controller.
A visitId that resolves to null throws IllegalArgumentException naming the ids, matching the owner-not-found and pet-not-found throws already in loadPetWithVisit.

The success path calls this.owners.save(owner) only. The bound Visit is the instance already inside owner -> pet -> visits, so CascadeType.ALL persists the edit in place. Do not call addVisit, and do not re-fetch the owner in the handler.

No template change is expected. createOrUpdateVisitForm already branches on visit['new']: a persisted visit renders the heading without 'New' and shows the previous-visits table. The form has no th:action, so it posts back to the /edit URL.
No new message-bundle key. I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync fails the build unless a new key is added to every locale bundle.

patterns.description: findPet: optional @PathVariable on a shared @ModelAttribute method, branching between the new and the edit mapping. The pattern to copy for visitId.
getPet(Integer): id lookup within the aggregate, returning null when absent. The shape for the new Pet.getVisit(Integer).
processUpdateForm: GET init, POST process, redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success, redisplay the view on binding errors.

VIEWS_PETS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM: the view-name constant convention. VisitController repeats the literal three times today and would reach five; extracting it is a fair Refactor step, not a requirement.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit runs before every handler in the controller. If it still calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()) on the edit path, the pet gains a phantom visit that the success-path save persists. This breaks the acceptance criterion that the pet has no visit it did not have before, and it also makes the GET form show a blank visit instead of the booked one.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId inside loadPetWithVisit. Construct and add a Visit only when visitId is null. Assert the pet's visit count is unchanged in the success test.

risks.risk: Repeating the non-future-date check verbatim in the second handler reads as a new business rule in a web controller. architecture-principles.md is explicit that the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules, so a reviewer can fail it.
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check from processNewVisitForm into one private method on VisitController and call it from both handlers. The controller's rule count stays at one; the rule is factored, not duplicated. Do not add @Future to Visit.date: that changes the booking flow's error code away from typeMismatch.visitDate and breaks its existing test.

risks.risk: Spring binds the submitted values onto the Visit instance before validation runs, so on a validation failure the in-memory visit already carries the rejected description or date. A test asserting 'the visit is unchanged' against the in-memory object will fail.
risks.mitigation: Assert the refusal as 'nothing was persisted': verify(owners, never()).save(any()) alongside the field-error and view-name expectations. The record is unchanged because no save happened, which is what the acceptance criterion means here.

risks.risk: A visitId belonging to another pet or another owner could be corrected through a mismatched URL.
risks.mitigation: Resolving the visit from pet.getVisits() within the single owner graph loaded in loadPetWithVisit makes the mismatch unresolvable by construction. Each request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the path, satisfying security-principles.md 'Trusting cross-request state'. The existing @InitBinder disallows id and *.id for every binder in the controller, so the visit identity comes from the path only, never the form.

risks.risk: Visit sits in a LinkedHashSet with @OrderBy("date ASC"). Mutating a member of a hash-based collection is normally a hazard.
risks.mitigation: Safe here: BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so set membership is by identity and is unaffected by the date change. No removal and re-add is needed.

notes: Test setup: the existing @BeforeEach builds an Owner with one Pet and no visits. Add a persisted-looking Visit (setId, setDate, setDescription) to the pet for the four correction tests, and keep the four booking tests unchanged as the regression guard on the null-visitId branch. Three open questions, each recorded rather than resolved, all taking the narrowest reading. First, the submit button on the correction form reads 'Add Visit' via the addVisit key; correcting the wording needs a new key in all twelve locale bundles, which exceeds this slice. Second, no confirmation flash message is added on the correction redirect: no acceptance criterion asks for one, and booking's message is a hardcoded English literal that REQ-LANG-002 disallows, so this slice declines to extend that pattern. Third, the previous-visits table on the correction page lists the visit being corrected. The PRD's open question about a correction reached through the wrong owner or pet is answered by construction, not by a new check: resolution through the owner-pet-visit graph refuses it on the same path booking already uses. No ADR is warranted; the product decision is already recorded in the narrowing ADR, and no how-decision here is hard to reverse or surprising. docs/system-design.md is deliberately not edited now, since it states current state and the code does not exist yet. At doc-sync the VisitController Contracts row must gain REQ-VIS-003 in its Implements column with its purpose widened beyond booking, and the Pet and Owner rows must pick up REQ-VIS-003 where the graph carries the correction. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Mass assignment into the owner aggregate through the visit routes. processUpdateVisitForm takes `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` — Spring resolves it from the model attribute loadPetWithVisit put there, then binds the POST body onto that entity — and the handler ends with `this.owners.save(owner)`. The controller's single `@InitBinder` disallows only `id` and `*.id`, so every other property of the aggregate is bindable and is then persisted: a POST to /owners/1/pets/1/visits/1/edit carrying firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone, or indexed nested fields such as pets[0].name rewrites the owner's record while nominally correcting a visit. createOrUpdateVisitForm.html submits only date, description and a hidden petId, so no owner field is ever a legitimate parameter on these routes — the binding surface is entirely unintended. Class sweep over the review surface: two instances, both in VisitController — the new processUpdateVisitForm (:135) and the pre-existing processNewVisitForm (:111), which the diff also touched. The same shape exists in PetController (outside this change set) and is not part of this finding. Severity is fixable rather than critical because the application has no authentication or authorization at all (docs/system-design.md Security Context), so an attacker crosses no privilege boundary that /owners/{id}/edit does not already grant openly — this is a least-privilege deviation in new code, not an escalation path. It should not ship in code written today.
findings.fix: Add a per-attribute binder alongside the existing one so the owner model attribute is never bound from the request, and narrow the existing binder to the visit: `@InitBinder("owner") void initOwnerBinder(WebDataBinder dataBinder) { dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("*"); }`. Keep the current `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` for the visit attribute (rename it `@InitBinder("visit")`), matching the per-attribute binder pattern PetController already uses. Both visit handlers then read the owner strictly as the loaded aggregate.

findings.description: The Threat Model records mass assignment as mitigated because "every controller's data binder explicitly disallows `id` and nested `id` binding". The finding above shows that mitigation covers identifier tampering only: non-id properties of a request-bound, then-persisted aggregate remain fully bindable. The row overstates the coverage, and a reviewer reading it would clear exactly the code path at issue. Worth restating the row as scoped to identifier tampering, with non-id form binding named as unmitigated where a handler saves a model-resolved aggregate.

approved_aspects: Visit resolution is correctly scoped through the owner→pet→visit graph: Pet.getVisit(id) walks only that pet's visits, so a visitId belonging to another pet or another owner resolves to null and is refused. No IDOR — the path variables cannot be recombined to reach a foreign visit.
No injection surface added: persistence stays on Spring Data JPA derived methods and cascade through save(owner); no string-concatenated SQL, no dynamic query construction.

No XSS introduced: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders the corrected date and description through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping; no th:utext, no inlined JavaScript, no unescaped URL fragment built from the new visitId.

Validation is not weakened on the correction path: rejectDateNotInTheFuture is the extracted form of the booking rule and is applied to both handlers, and @Valid still enforces the entity constraints; the refusal path returns the form without calling save, so a rejected correction cannot reach persistence.
Secrets sweep over the diff (token, password, secret, key, credential, api-key) returns no hardcoded credential; the only hit is prose in docs/prd.md about message-bundle keys.
Supply chain: the change set touches no build file (no build.gradle, pom.xml, or lockfile), so the pass introduces no dependency delta and no new transitive surface to verify against the NVD.

architectural_fit: Unchanged from line 8. The correction is a third server-rendered form flow in the owner feature package, alongside owner edit and pet edit. integration_points: Carried forward from line 8 unchanged: the GET and POST edit mappings, the optional visitId on loadPetWithVisit, Pet.getVisit(Integer), the not-found throw, save-only on the success path, no template change, no new message-bundle key.

New. VisitController gains @InitBinder("owner") calling setDisallowedFields("*"), and the existing class-wide @InitBinder is renamed @InitBinder("visit") keeping setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"). The owner is then read strictly as the aggregate loadPetWithVisit loaded, never as form input. This is the security reviewer's proposed fix and I rule it architecturally right: the visit form offers no owner field, so disallowing all of them is least privilege stated at the binding boundary, and the per-attribute shape is already the codebase's idiom in PetController.

The rename is required rather than optional. Two binders that both match the owner attribute would each call setDisallowedFields, and the second call replaces the first rather than merging. Spring guarantees no ordering between @InitBinder methods, so keeping a class-wide binder alongside a named one makes the effective disallow list non-deterministic.
After the rename the controller has no class-wide default binder. Every model attribute a handler binds in this controller needs its own named binder; today that is owner and visit only.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass-assignment hole closed on BOTH visit handlers: @InitBinder("owner") with setDisallowedFields("*") is selected by model-attribute name, so it applies to every handler in VisitController binding "owner" - processNewVisitForm and processUpdateVisitForm alike. "*" matches through PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch, so nested and indexed paths (pets[0].name) are disallowed too. VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionShouldNotChangeTheOwnersDetails pins firstName, telephone, and pets[0].name against the saved aggregate; no further instance of the class exists in the change set.

Identifier tampering closed on the visit attribute: @InitBinder("visit") disallows "id" and "*.id", so a submitted id cannot repoint the correction at another visit. The visit identity comes only from the {visitId} path variable.

Object-reference integrity on the new edit route: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId), and Pet.getVisit skips new visits and matches by id within that pet only. A visitId belonging to another pet or owner cannot be reached; the negative test asserts the refusal and that no save occurs.

No new injection surface: the new route takes only int/Integer path variables and the existing date/description form fields. Persistence stays on Spring Data JPA derived methods; no string-concatenated SQL or JPQL added.
Output escaping intact: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders every user-derived value through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping; no th:utext anywhere under templates/.
Validation is applied identically on both paths: @Valid Visit plus the shared rejectDateNotInTheFuture, with tests asserting the visit is unchanged and no save happens on refusal.
No secrets in the diff: the only credential-shaped literals are test fixture constants (a sample telephone number); no token, key, password, or connection string added.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle and the lock/BOM surface are untouched by the change set, so no new direct or transitive dependency enters. No OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle, so dependencyCheckAnalyze is not available; the check reduces to confirming zero dependency delta.

Threat model now records the split accurately: an identifier-tampering row (mitigated) and a separate non-identifier mass-assignment row that stays qualified for the controllers whose owner binder still disallows identifiers only.
